stories.title: Significant drop in levels of toxic 'forever' chemicals in England's rivers
summary: The decline has been put down to severe restrictions placed on the substances' use.

stories.title: 'Summer was a wake-up call, winter could be dire' warning over food supplies
summary: Wales needs to grow more fruit and veg or it will be at the mercy of wars and climate change, says expert.

stories.title: Toby Jones stars in film about UK Mars mission
summary: Mackenzie Crook directs the story of the British professor whose probe lost contact upon touchdown.

stories.title: The mystery of how hair knows where to grow may finally be solved
summary: Scientists have discovered that the intricate patterns of hair follicles on mammals may arise from a remarkably simple process involving cells following chemical signals.
The findings challenge a long-standing theory and reveal how nature can create complex biological patterns without a detailed blueprint.

stories.title: NASA reveals Earth's ozone hole has grown to a size not seen in a decade
summary: The Antarctic ozone hole expanded to its seventh-largest size on record in 2026, driven by unusual weather conditions that pushed it close to its historic maximum.
Scientists say international restrictions on ozone-destroying chemicals prevented even greater damage, and Earth's protective ozone layer is still recovering.

stories.title: Scientists find deadly virus DNA hidden in 1,000-year-old manuscripts
summary: Ancient manuscripts, including the 1,000-year-old York Gospels, have revealed traces of a deadly sheep virus whose history stretches back more than 3,700 years.
Scientists discovered that the virus has remained remarkably unchanged for millennia, turning historic parchment into an unexpected record of ancient disease outbreaks.

stories.title: Scientists uncover a 192-year-old mystery hidden in a mangled silver coin
summary: A bizarrely deformed 1834 British silver coin found at a car boot sale may preserve evidence of a rare minting accident nearly 200 years ago.
Advanced 3D scans and microscopic analysis revealed unusual metal distortions suggesting the coin was crushed under extreme pressure, potentially during its original production.

stories.title: Where are all the males? Ancient human fossils reveal a startling mystery
summary: A remarkable discovery in a South African cave suggests that an extinct human relative may have created an all-female burial site more than 240,000 years ago.

Scientists analyzed ancient proteins preserved in Homo naledi teeth and found no male-specific markers among at least 20 individuals, potentially solving a mystery that has puzzled researchers for over a decade.

stories.title: A radical theory says the universe is twice as old as we thought
summary: A provocative new cosmological model suggests the Universe could be 26.7 billion years old and might not need dark matter or dark energy to explain its behavior.

University of Ottawa researchers tested the theory against several major astronomical observations, finding that it could explain galaxy rotation, cosmic expansion, and the formation of early elements.

stories.title: Bid to restore rare Atlantic rainforest secures £6m lottery grant
summary: Hubs offering training in conservation work are to be set up in Torridon, Morvern and mid-Argyll.

stories.title: Artist creates world's biggest soil painting
summary: Phil Lambert used four types of soil, including some collected from his mother, to create his work.

stories.title: Scientists discover why some mosquitoes love you and others don't
summary: A surprising new study reveals that mosquitoes have very different tastes in humans, with each species attracted to its own combination of skin odors, chemicals, and bacteria.
The discovery challenges the idea of a universal mosquito magnet and could lead to more effective repellents against dangerous disease-spreading mosquitoes.

stories.title: Scientists discover a giant 66-pound rodent that lived 34 million years ago
summary: Scientists have uncovered fossils of a giant rodent that lived in Thailand 34 million years ago, revealing that enormous rodents evolved much earlier than previously thought.
Named Yakamys sirindhornae, the ancient animal may have weighed around 66 pounds, roughly twice as much as other known rodents of its time.

stories.title: 237-million-year-old fossils reveal a bizarre armored sea amphibian
summary: A bizarre, heavily armored amphibian roamed the oceans 237 million years ago, despite the fact that modern amphibians cannot survive entirely in saltwater.
Discovered in China, the giant salamander-sized creature may be the first known amphibian to have adapted to a fully marine existence.

stories.title: Duchy tenants may have to buy farms or leave as Prince William plans sell-off
summary: A ten-year strategy to raise £500m from the Duchy of Cornwall will see farms sold off across England.

stories.title: Astronomers discover hidden alien planet in James Webb images
summary: A breakthrough in telescope imaging could reveal countless alien worlds that have been hiding in plain sight.

Scientists developed a new technique that uses a digital twin of the James Webb Space Telescope to remove the overwhelming glare of stars, making faint exoplanets two to 15 times easier to detect than with conventional methods.
The technology has already uncovered a previously hidden planet in existing telescope data and could reveal many more.
